question.worked_solution:
The period of $y=\operatorname{sec}⁡x$ is $2\pi .$ Therefore, for integer $n$ we have

$$
\operatorname{sec}⁡x=\operatorname{sec}⁡(x+2n\pi ).
$$

Substituting $n=-9$ into the right-hand-side of the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sec}⁡x=\operatorname{sec}⁡(x+2\cdot (-9)\cdot \pi )=\operatorname{sec}⁡(x-18\pi ).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, if $\operatorname{sec}⁡x=\frac{7}{6},$ then $\operatorname{sec}⁡(x-18\pi )=\frac{7}{6}.$

Finally, then

$$
\begin{aligned}18\operatorname{sec}⁡(x-18\pi )+2 & =18(\frac{7}{6})+2 \\  & =21+2 \\  & =23.\end{aligned}
$$
